title: Safely reconcile a vCenter VM CPU count after an ambiguous mutation
prompt:
Platform engineering needs a retry-safe way to converge a virtual machine on a requested CPU count when a mutating response may be ambiguous. Complete `VcfVcenterCpuReconciler/VcfVcenterCpuReconciler.psm1`.

Read the protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The focused contract was projected directly from `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the immutable VCF 9.1 commit recorded in both files. The YAML specification, not a rendered documentation page, is the wire authority. The exact operationIds in scope are `Vcenter.Vm.Hardware.Cpu_get` and `Vcenter.Vm.Hardware.Cpu_update`.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 is installed by the environment. Keep the supplied manifest prerequisite on `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` version `13.5.0.25380678`; it supplies the OpenAPI server-connection contract used by the module. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, or replace any VMware module, SDK assembly, binding, or OpenAPI file. Issue the requests as `System.Net.Http.HttpRequestMessage` messages sent through `System.Net.Http.HttpClient`; the implementation must not contain `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, `Start-Process`, `curl`, or `Connect-VIServer`.

Preserve the supplied signatures and export exactly these commands:

- `New-VcfVcenterCpuClient` accepts either an authenticated `VMware.Sdk.OpenApi.Cmdlets.IServerConnection` (with an optional `-Server` URI override) or the loopback-friendly `-Server <uri> -SessionToken <string>` form. In the connection form, reuse the HTTP client returned by the connection's `.GetClient()` method. `-SkipCertificateCheck` belongs only to the token form. Creating a client performs no API request.
- `Set-VcfVmCpuCount -Client <object> -Vm <string> -Count <int64>` converges one VM on a positive CPU count.

For every invocation, first send `GET /api/vcenter/vm/{vm}/hardware/cpu`. Percent-encode the VM path value with `[uri]::EscapeDataString`. Reject a null or malformed successful response: `count`, `cores_per_socket`, `hot_add_enabled`, and `hot_remove_enabled` are all required; both counts must be positive integers and both flags must be booleans. If the returned count already equals `Count`, do not mutate. Return an object with `Vm`, `PreviousCount`, `Count`, and `Changed` (`false`).

If the returned count differs, send exactly one `PATCH` to the same path with JSON media type and the compact body `{"count":<requested integer>}`. The update specification's `cores_per_socket`, `hot_add_enabled`, and `hot_remove_enabled` properties are unset and must be omitted, not sent as null, zero, an empty string, or false. On a successful PATCH return the same result shape with the observed old count, requested count, and `Changed` set to `true`.

Send `Accept: application/json`, authenticate with `vmware-api-session-id`, send no query string, and fail every non-2xx response. Do not blindly repeat a PATCH within an invocation after an error: the server may have applied the mutation even when its response was unsuccessful. A caller retry is safe because a fresh invocation performs GET again and skips PATCH once the desired count is observed.

Run `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File .protected/verify.ps1`. The protected verifier creates runtime-only identifiers and credentials, starts the contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, and reads its fsynced request log. The mock applies the first PATCH but returns HTTP 503. The verifier confirms that the first invocation surfaces the error, the retry observes the applied state, and no duplicate PATCH targets that desired count. It separately exercises a successful 204 update and its stable retry. It also checks the exact method, encoded path, absent query, authentication and media headers, body bytes, result, and omission of every unset update field. It never contacts a live VMware endpoint. Everything under `.protected/` and `docs/`, plus the module manifest, is protected; edit only `VcfVcenterCpuReconciler/VcfVcenterCpuReconciler.psm1`.
scenario: the vCenter mock applies a count-only CPU update but returns HTTP 503, so a caller retry must re-read the VM, recognize the desired count, and avoid a duplicate mutation
constraint: the loopback fixture derives its sole path and two allowed methods from the protected contract, and its fsynced log proves the exact encoded target, headers, body bytes, one-mutation retry behavior, and omission of every unset update field
